texts.facts: All these petitions are filed by the petitioners for the accidental injuries sustained by them in the road accident dated 17.01.2023. The petitioner in MVC No.1631/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-, MVC No.1632/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-, MVC No.1633/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- and petitioner in MVC No. 1634/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents with interest. The first respondent had been willfully entrusted their vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of the accident. Immediately, the petitioners were shifted to New Manasa Hospital for first aid treatment and further shifted to Aveksha Hospital, Bangalore, wherein they were treated as inpatient.
texts.arguments: 15 . In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in SCCH-21 13 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The learned counsel for contesting respondent argued Yashavanth M.E vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82152578/ 10 that, all the petitioners claimed medical bill through their college and driver of the Omini vehicle not taken proper care to run the said vehicle. 29. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the Yashavanth M.E vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82152578/ 16 evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head. He was sworn that, petitioner has got 12% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.

From perusal of the copy of policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 03.10.2022 to 02.10.2023.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 17.01.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, as respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
44. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance C
By relying on the aforesaid decision, 6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
